Audit result: NO-GO for automated Herdr adoption. Herdr is suitable for a later manual hosting/UX pilot only after an explicit single-authority handoff. The evidence is complete enough for that decision, but not for authorization to pilot.

Installed reality:

- Binary: `/home/deploy/.local/bin/herdr`
- Version/channel/protocol: `0.8.2`, stable, protocol 20
- Linux x86_64 static PIE, 22,733,040 bytes
- SHA-256: `976150a14d490c94b243ea2e1a7eb2dfb67f12e36b182db90936f6728e6aecf4`
- Build ID: `481cefd16bb9edffae7ce54a8f5ba1c549e259a5`
- Exact hash matches the official v0.8.2 Linux asset, proving release provenance. [Official release metadata](https://herdr.dev/latest.json)
- Source: [herdrdev/herdr v0.8.2](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/tree/v0.8.2); docs: [Herdr documentation](https://herdr.dev/docs/). No local source checkout was found in the searched application/source directories.
- Direct-installed binary; not present in the global npm package inventory.

Runtime inventory:

- Default sockets exist at `/home/deploy/.config/herdr/herdr.sock` and `herdr-client.sock`, mode 0600.
- Server log records server PID `2585062`, pane PIDs `2585072` and `2585076`, and Codex PGID `2586376`.
- During the audit, external client PID `2597200` attached and closed workspace `w5`; pane PID `2585072` exited. This child issued no close, stop, attach, or input command.
- Final persisted state contains one workspace: `w7`, cwd `/home/deploy`, one pane, no exact durable-supervisor repository workspace.
- No Herdr systemd unit file was found in the inspected system/user unit paths. Bus, socket, tmux, and host `/proc` access were sandbox-denied.
- There is no later server-shutdown log entry, but current process liveness cannot be proven from this namespace. `herdr session list` reporting “stopped” is therefore not authoritative.
- Opsle remains `AUTHORITATIVE`, identity `supervisor-1005d601-4da1-4f6b-a7fa-f0b71dedabbe`, generation 9, state `DORMANT`. Tmux liveness is likewise unproven because its socket was denied.

Capability matrix:

| Primitive | Evidence/classification |
|---|---|
| Workspace/tab/pane | Structured IDs, topology, cwd, revisions, focus and terminal IDs through `api snapshot`, `workspace list/get`, `pane list/get/layout`. |
| Repository metadata | Structured worktree provenance: repo key/name/root, checkout path and linked-worktree flag. `workspace.report-metadata` supports display-only tokens with sequence and TTL. |
| Process | `pane process-info` returns shell PID, foreground PGID and process PID/name/argv/cwd. It lacks executable identity, process start ticks, parent chain and generation. |
| Agent | Structured `AgentInfo`, native session reference and lifecycle state. Codex lifecycle is explicitly screen-manifest-derived, not a native prompt/composer contract. [Agent status authority](https://herdr.dev/docs/agents/) |
| Events | `events.subscribe` and `events.wait` are structured and event-driven. Envelopes lack durable event IDs, cursors, sequence numbers and replay guarantees. |
| Wait | `agent.wait` pins the resolved occupant; `agent.prompt` can combine submission and wait, avoiding only the prompt/wait race. Pane output waits are screen-text matching. |
| Prompt/input | `agent.prompt` request is `{target,text,wait?}` and ultimately sends PTY text plus Enter. It rejects an already-blocked agent but may send from other non-working or working states. Raw pane send methods are PTY transport only. |
| Attach/detach | Full UI attach, SSH remote attach, and direct agent/terminal attach exist. Direct attach permits one writable controller plus multiple read-only observers; this does not exclude full UI or API input. [Persistence and remote attach](https://herdr.dev/docs/persistence-remote/) |
| Sidebar/multi-client | Strong operational fit: workspaces and agent states appear in the sidebar, metadata tokens are display-only, and multiple clients are supported. |

Native safety guarantees:

- Prompt idle: no
- Empty human draft: no
